5b-from-hybrid.text: Blockage in the bypass line (e.g., debris) — Blockage prevents steam flow, starving reboiler E-1B of heat and causing process disturbance.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Atmospheric tank leaks — Release of anhydrous ammonia gas to the atmosphere, creating a toxic vapor cloud that poses inhalation hazard to personnel and potential environmental release.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: A significant release of anhydrous ammonia from the fertiliser plant's tank could create a toxic vapor cloud causing a single fatality or several serious injuries on site; off-site impact is uncertain due to distance (residences >400 m) and ammonia's buoyancy, but not ruled out.

5b-from-hybrid.text: External heat source (fire, steam tracing) causing overpressure of ammonia tank — Increase in tank pressure leading to relief valve release or tank rupture, releasing anhydrous ammonia gas (toxic, irritant) to surrounding area.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: External heat (fire) could cause tank rupture and a large ammonia release, with consequences similar to an atmospheric leak: potential for a single fatality or several serious injuries on site; off-site effects uncertain.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Water intrusion (e.g., washdown, leak) into ammonia tank — Rapid dissolution of ammonia in water generating heat and ammonium hydroxide solution; possible pressure rise and release of ammonia vapour or heat.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Water intrusion causes exothermic dissolution and possible pressure rise with ammonia vapour release; a significant release could still cause a single fatality or several serious injuries on site, though the scenario may be less violent than fire-induced rupture.

5b-from-hybrid.text: External fire heating the tank wall increasing ammonia vapor pressure — Pressure rise above design limit could cause tank rupture or relief valve discharge, releasing anhydrous ammonia to the pipe rack above and surrounding area.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Tank rupture or relief discharge releases large ammonia quantity to pipe rack and area; significant release, could cause multiple serious injuries on site. Facts: T-NH3 contains AMMONIA.

5b-from-hybrid.text: External fire or steam heating raising tank temperature — Higher temperature increases ammonia vapor pressure, potentially leading to overpressure, tank rupture, and ammonia release to the pipe rack above and surroundings.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Temperature rise leads to overpressure, tank rupture, ammonia release to pipe rack and surroundings; significant on-site hazard. Facts: T-NH3 contains AMMONIA.

5b-from-hybrid.text: External fire heating the tank or blocked vent leading to pressure rise — Tank overpressure could cause rupture, releasing MNT liquid/vapour to surroundings
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Tank rupture from overpressure (T-PMNT.contents) releases MNT liquid/vapour; significant release could cause fire/toxicity reaching occupied control room 50 ft (LOC-P-CONTROL-ROOM); single fatality or several serious injuries on site plausible.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Loss of cooling to T-PMNT causing heating of stored MNT — Pressure and temperature build-up in T-PMNT due to exothermic reaction of MNT stored at elevated temperature
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Exothermic reaction of MNT (T-PMNT.contents) at elevated temperature leads to pressure/temperature build-up and potential tank failure; significant release of flammable/toxic MNT could affect control room 50 ft (LOC-P-CONTROL-ROOM); single fatality or several serious injuries on site.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Wrong charge of chlorine into ammonia tank (T-NH3) or leak allowing mixing — Ammonia and chlorine react to form chloramines (e.g., monochloramine) and potentially nitrogen trichloride, releasing toxic, irritating gases; risk of explosion if nitrogen trichloride forms.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Ammonia (T-NH3.contents) and chlorine form toxic chloramines and potentially explosive nitrogen trichloride; toxic gas release and explosion risk in tank area; could cause single fatality or several serious injuries on site; reactivity not_listed but known chemistry.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Wrong charge of toluene into ammonia equipment — Ammonia and toluene can react exothermically, potentially releasing heat and possibly forming hazardous products such as benzylamine or other alkylated amines.
5b-from-hybrid.severity_reason: Wrong toluene charge into ammonia tank T-NH3 causes exothermic reaction (specialist), potentially hazardous products; tank rupture could release large quantities of flammable toluene and toxic ammonia to plant personnel. Facts: T-NH3.contents, T-NH3.type, reactivity not_listed but specialist_conseq.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Heat exchanger tube ruptures — Process fluid leaks from tube bundle into the shell side or into steam space, mixing with the heating medium and changing composition.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Residual water remaining in reflux cooler E-2 after draining for tube work — Water mixed with MNT could lead to hydrolysis, corrosion, or slug flow, potentially damaging equipment and causing overpressure that activates PSV-1.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Loss of cooling in reflux cooler E-2 leads to overheating and flashing of MNT to vapor in the line — Elevated temperature causes partial vaporization of MNT, resulting in two‑phase flow, possible pressure increase, and activation of PSV-1.

5b-from-hybrid.text: External heating causing MNT to boil/vaporize — Vapor generation could increase pressure, potentially leading to venting or tank overpressure.

5b-from-hybrid.text: Wrong charge of formaldehyde into ammonia tank (T-NH3) or mixing during cleaning — Ammonia and formaldehyde can react to form hexamethylenetetramine (hexamine) and water, releasing heat; possible irritant vapours but no highly toxic products.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-temperature trip on reboiler E-1A that closes a new steam supply block valve (XV-SS-A) upstream of both FV-A and SS-A-BYPASS.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for the combined FV-A fail-open and SS-A-BYPASS left-open deviations. An independent trip on E-1A isolating steam at a single upstream point mitigates both paths simultaneously, preferred over procedural control of the bypass which would not address FV-A failure.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-temperature trip on reboiler E-1A that closes a new steam supply block valve (XV-SS-A) upstream of both FV-A and SS-A-BYPASS.
recommendations.reason: Same root cause (FV-A fail open) affects line SS-A; the independent high-temperature trip on E-1A closing steam supply upstream of both paths also protects the line, so this action serves both C1 and L1.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-temperature trip on column C-1 that closes the steam supply to reboiler E-1A (valve FV-A or new block valve XV-SS-C1) when C-1 temperature exceeds 374°F, and revise PROC-P-C1-OPERATING-1 to enforce a 374°F limit and mandatory nitrogen purge before opening C-1.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist for MNT decomposition from air/heat exposure. The engineered trip directly removes the heat hazard at the decomposition threshold, while the procedural revision addresses the air ingress cause; together they close the gap more reliably than either alone.

recommendations.action: Revise operating procedure PROC-P-C1-OPERATING-1 to include mandatory nitrogen purge and step-sequence enforcement (e.g., checklist sign-off) before any operation that could expose MNT in C-1 to air.
recommendations.reason: The cause is purely procedural (operator skips steps); no engineered layer exists. Revising the procedure to enforce nitrogen purge and step sequence removes the cause directly, preferred over adding an alarm that relies on operator response.

recommendations.action: Install a redundant flow sensor on steam line SS-A and implement 2-out-of-3 voting logic for FV-A control to prevent a single erroneous sensor signal from driving the valve closed.
recommendations.reason: The cause is a single sensor/controller wrong signal; no protection layers exist. Adding sensor redundancy with voting removes the cause at the source, preferred over a low-flow alarm which would only detect the consequence.

recommendations.action: Install a material verification interlock on MNT transfer lines L-MNT-TANK-STRIPPER and L-MNT-STRIPPER-C1 requiring independent lab confirmation of MNT identity before allowing charge to column C-1.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for wrong-material charging. This engineered interlock removes the cause by preventing transfer until composition is verified, which is more reliable than procedural checks or alarms alone.

recommendations.action: Fit independent limit switches with control-room alarm and automatic closure interlock on all sulfuric acid block valves feeding MNT-containing equipment, keyed to operating procedure PROC-P-C1-OPERATING-1.
recommendations.reason: No layers guard against a valve left open to sulfuric acid. Position sensors with auto-closure provide an engineered barrier that acts on the deviation (wrong valve position) independent of operator memory or procedure compliance.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-temperature trip on reboiler E-1B shell outlet (TSH-E1B) that automatically closes steam supply valve SS-B-INLET, independent of control valve FV-B and bypass valve SS-B-BYPASS.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist for the bypass-valve-left-open scenario. A temperature trip on the heated equipment detects the consequence (overheating) directly and acts on the steam source, independent of the failed control loop and manual valve.

recommendations.action: Install an independent low-flow switch on reflux line L-C1-E2 (FSL-C1-E2) that alarms and triggers standby reflux pump start or alternate flow path, independent of pump P-C1-REFLUX status and the manual outlet block valve.
recommendations.reason: No layers address the dual loss of reflux flow. A flow switch detects the deviation (no flow) itself, not its causes, and initiates recovery regardless of whether the pump tripped or the valve was closed.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high-pressure trip on column C-1 bottoms (PSH-C1-BOTTOMS) that closes both steam inlet valves SS-A-INLET and SS-B-INLET, independent of control valves FV-A/FV-B and condensate line L-E1A-CONDENSATE.
recommendations.reason: PSV-1 alone leaves a 100× gap. An instrumented trip on the protected vessel acts earlier than relief, isolates the heat sources directly, and is independent of the failed control valves and blocked condensate return.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high-temperature trip (TSH) on C-1 bottom that closes steam inlet valves SS-A-INLET and SS-B-INLET.
recommendations.reason: PSV-1 only relieves at design pressure; an independent trip on the temperature deviation acts earlier and independently of the failed control valves FV-A/FV-B, closing the steam source.

recommendations.action: Add an independent high-pressure trip (PSH) on C-1 at a set point below PSV-1 that closes steam inlet valves SS-A-INLET and SS-B-INLET.
recommendations.reason: PSV-1 credited but gap remains; an independent pressure trip provides a layer that acts on overpressure before relief, independent of temperature instruments TI-B/TI-R and control valves.

recommendations.action: Revise PROC-P-C1-ESD-1 to require closing and locking steam supply isolation valves SS-A-INLET, SS-B-INLET, SS-A-BYPASS, and SS-B-BYPASS, and verify condensate return path open.
recommendations.reason: Current procedure leaves steam path open downstream of FV-A/B; if steam restored, reboilers become fired vessels. Closing all inlet valves removes the hazard at source.

recommendations.action: Install an independent high-pressure trip (PSH) on C-1 at a set point below PSV-1 (e.g., 10 psig) that closes steam inlet valves SS-A-INLET and SS-B-INLET.
recommendations.reason: PSV-1 is not credited as it is the failing component in the chain; an independent pressure trip provides a credited layer that acts before relief.

recommendations.action: Install a fail-closed block valve on nitrogen line L-N2-C1 at the C-1 connection, interlocked to an independent high-pressure switch (PSH) on C-1.
recommendations.reason: PSV-1 not credited; preventing nitrogen entry at source with an automatic valve removes the cause, and the interlock provides an independent engineered layer.
